issues.title: Claim that the test's loopback sink can't batch flushes is factually wrong
issues.verdictReason: loopback_data_sink_impl::can_batch_flushes() (tests/unit/loopback_socket.hh:164) returns true, and connected_socket::output() (src/net/stack.cc:116-121) unconditionally sets opts.batch_flushes=true, so output_stream::_batch_flushes is true for this stream's write_buf; send_entry() calls write_buf.flush() after every write (src/rpc/rpc.cc:188), so the batch-flush/_in_batch path is genuinely exercised, contradicting the claim.
issues.scopeReason: the test and its comments are new code added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The regression test never exercises the batch-flush path it describes. The loopback sink it wraps does not support batch flushes, so the stream's write_buf flushes synchronously and the ~output_stream `!_in_batch` crash cannot occur in this test.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-six-pass-batched-2026-10-08/ironwea: The regression test never exercises the batch-flush path it describes. The loopback sink it wraps does not support batch flushes, so the stream's write_buf flushes synchronously and the ~output_stream `!_in_batch` crash cannot occur in this test.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Two test comments describe behavior that never happens in this fixture: the 'batch flush poller' yield loop and the closing note that ~output_stream() asserts on a pending batch flush.

issues.title: Test doesn't assert send_empty_frame hook was refused; relies only on a side effect
issues.verdictReason: The try/catch around stream_send_empty_frame().get() (rpc_test.cc:2016-2020) only reacts to rpc::closed_error; a successful call falls through silently. The regression is still caught later via BOOST_REQUIRE_MESSAGE(!st.put_after_close, ...) at line 2030, so the test does fail on a regression, but not at the point the comments imply, and not with a clear assertion about the exception itself.
issues.scopeReason: new test code added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The test does not assert that the send_empty_frame hook was refused with closed_error. A hook that succeeds is silently accepted.

issues.title: No test covers stream_close() draining pre-existing queued entries
issues.verdictReason: In the new test, every send() completes (.get()) before stream_close() runs, so _outgoing_queue is always empty when stream_close() exchanges _outgoing_queue_ready at rpc.cc:562; no test creates an in-flight entry racing the _stream_closing flag, so that drain path is never meaningfully exercised.
issues.scopeReason: the drain logic is new code from this PR and the new test is the only coverage added for it.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: No test covers the second half of the fix: stream_close() waiting for _outgoing_queue_ready to drain entries accepted before _stream_closing was set.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-six-pass-batched-2026-10-08/ironwea: No test covers the second half of the fix: stream_close() waiting for _outgoing_queue_ready to drain entries accepted before _stream_closing was set.

issues.title: Doc overstates that any exception while reading a source closes it
issues.verdictReason: source_impl::operator()() (include/seastar/rpc/rpc_impl.hh:941-983) only calls close_source() when stream_receive() itself fails or yields eof; an exception thrown by unmarshall() while deserializing an already-buffered frame (process_one_buffer(), line 945-948) propagates without calling close_source(), so 'throws is what closes it' is false for that case.
issues.scopeReason: this is new documentation text added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The new docs say any exception thrown while reading a source closes it. That is false for exceptions thrown while deserializing a buffer.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-six-pass-batched-2026-10-08/ironwea: The new docs say any exception thrown while reading a source closes it. That is false for exceptions thrown while deserializing a buffer.

issues.title: Doc claim that a stream connection shuts down 'only once both halves are closed' is…
issues.verdictReason: client::abort_all_streams() (src/rpc/rpc.cc:848-855) calls abort() directly on every child stream connection when the parent client closes, shutting it down without either half of the stream protocol being closed; this contradicts the unqualified statement at doc/rpc-streaming.md:115, even though the doc separately (lines 49-51) already describes client-close as aborting streams.
issues.scopeReason: new documentation text added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The new doc says a stream's connection is shut down 'only once both halves are closed'. That contradicts the client-close abort described a few lines earlier and the error/peer-eof paths in the client loop.

issues.verdictReason: stop_send_loop() (rpc.cc:225) explicitly does when_all(std::move(_outgoing_queue_ready), ...); after stream_close()'s exchange at line 562 that future is always already-resolved, so the wait is vacuous in practice, but the comment's literal claim that 'nothing else waits for it' is not true of the code.
issues.scopeReason: new comment text added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The stream_close() comment says nothing else waits for _outgoing_queue_ready. In fact stop_send_loop() still awaits it, and suspend_for_testing() calls .get() on it.

issues.title: test_data_sink_impl::put override is not guarded by SEASTAR_API_LEVEL, unlike the repo's…
issues.verdictReason: data_sink_impl::put(std::span<...>) only exists when SEASTAR_API_LEVEL >= 9 (include/seastar/core/iostream.hh:110-128); below that level the pure virtual is put(net::packet). test_data_sink_impl (rpc_test.cc:1877-1888) overrides only the span form unconditionally, while tests/unit/loopback_socket.hh:144-153 guards the same choice with #if SEASTAR_API_LEVEL >= 9 / #else. Built with Seastar_API_LEVEL=7 (an explicitly supported CMake cache value), test_data_sink_impl would fail to compile as an abstract class missing put(net::packet). Default build (level 9) is unaffected.
issues.scopeReason: new test code added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: `test_data_sink_impl` unconditionally overrides `put(std::span<temporary_buffer<char>>)`, which exists only when `SEASTAR_API_LEVEL >= 9`. The repository's own loopback sink guards the same override with `#if`.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-six-pass-batched-2026-10-08/ironwea: `test_data_sink_impl` unconditionally overrides `put(std::span<temporary_buffer<char>>)`, which exists only when `SEASTAR_API_LEVEL >= 9`. The repository's own loopback sink guards the same override with `#if`.

issues.title: stream_close() comment wrongly implies failed sends make _outgoing_queue_ready exceptional
issues.verdictReason: In send()'s continuation (rpc.cc:333-339), when send_entry() fails it calls abort() and then unconditionally p->done.set_value() (not set_exception), so a failed send resolves the chain with a value, not an exception. The comment's 'exceptional if an entry failed' conflates that with withdraw()'s exception path (used by stop_send_loop/timeout cancellation), which is a different mechanism.
issues.scopeReason: new comment text added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The new `stream_close()` comment says `_outgoing_queue_ready` is exceptional "if an entry failed". In `send()`, a failed entry resolves its `done` promise with a value.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-six-pass-batched-2026-10-08/ironwea: The new `stream_close()` comment says `_outgoing_queue_ready` is exceptional "if an entry failed". In `send()`, a failed entry resolves its `done` promise with a value.

issues.title: stream_close() comment wrongly claims _error is only set by the stop() that follows
issues.verdictReason: _error can also be set independently on the same connection by stop_send_loop() (rpc.cc:199) or by abort() called directly from send()'s failure continuation (rpc.cc:336), neither of which is 'the stop() that follows' in stream_close(); either could race with stream_close() and set _error before stop() runs.
issues.scopeReason: new comment text added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The new stream_close() comment says _error is only set by the stop() that follows, but other paths on the same stream connection set it independently.
